facts.fact: ARCEP's half-year 2026 observatory says Starlink CAR obtained a licence to market and operate satellite fixed wireless internet in CAF (licence date not given; document published 2026-09-16).

ARCEP reports Starlink CAR officially launched satellite fixed wireless internet to users in Bangui in March 2026 and held over 70% of the 5,380 fixed wireless internet clients at end-June 2026 (Orange 29%), carrying over 22.89 million GB of traffic since March.

note: ARCEP gives no satellite-only subscriber count (5,380 is all fixed wireless, Orange included), so no counted fact.

facts.fact: ARCEP began an inspection operation in Bangui against unregistered Starlink kit users and Wi-Fi providers; the minister says over 3,000 people use Starlink kits illegally against 200 registered with ARCEP, and the sweep is to extend to provincial towns (article dated 2026-08-14, operation said to start 'Wednesday').

note: Enforcement against unregistered use, recorded as none.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Digital Economy, Posts and Telecommunications announced on 23 April 2026 the suspension (deactivation) of Starlink kits imported abroad and used in roaming mode, for lacking homologation; users are told to regularise with ARCEP.

A Ministry communiqué issued in Bangui in April 2026 suspended illegally imported Starlink kits operating in roaming mode, which had not met homologation conditions; roaming was deactivated pending regulatory review and users must approach ARCEP (article dated 2026-04-28).

note: Event date taken from publication; the communiqué gives only April 2026.

facts.fact: The ministry's December 2025 communiqué, cited by Agence Ecofin, followed the award of a licence to Starlink in CAF.

Starlink announced on 16 March 2026 the commercial availability of its service in CAF, in partnership with hardware distributor DEVEA Centrafrique, at 33,000 FCFA a month plus 19% VAT, with a standard kit at 240,000 FCFA and a Mini kit at 123,000 FCFA.

note: Signing of a government-Starlink agreement to complete installation; no licence, launch or sale stated.

facts.fact: Authorities suspended use of Starlink kits in roaming mode (devices bought abroad and used locally without national approval), as outside the regulatory framework; the document is dated 2026-04-28 and gives no earlier date for the suspension.
Starlink launched commercially in CAR in March 2026; a standard kit costs CFA240,000 and the monthly subscription CFA33,000 before taxes, and users can legally buy a kit locally.

Starlink launched commercially in Bangui on Monday (the week of the 19 March 2026 article) through a partnership between the government and DEVEA Centrafrique; standard kit about 265,000 CFA francs, monthly subscription 33,000 CFA francs, and 450 kits with 12-month subscriptions secured by the government.

note: Mentions Eutelsat OneWeb only as a pan-African rival, not as on sale in CAF.

facts.fact: On 16 March 2026 CAR officially launched commercialisation of Starlink through a partnership between the government and DEVEA Centrafrique, Starlink's local representative; V4 kit 262,305 to 265,000 FCFA excluding tax, residential subscription 33,000 FCFA a month.
The government approved Starlink's operating licence in December 2025, per the article.

Starlink launched in CAR, shown as available on Starlink's map, with a 33,000 CFA franc monthly residential package and a 240,000 CFA franc standard kit; the document gives no launch date, so its publication date is used.
Radio Ndeke Luka reports Starlink became officially operational in CAF with the launch of its activities in Bangui on 16 March 2026, with management granted to DEVEAG-Centrafrique.

note: Stub of an audio interview; text only says the minister discusses fibre and use of the Starlink satellite network, no dated licence or sale statement.

facts.fact: Space in Africa, citing the Ministry of Digital Economy, reports Starlink and the CAF government signed an agreement at a ceremony hosted by the President (article dated 2025-12-23) under which Starlink's network is to be made commercially available in CAF for the first time; the document calls it an agreement, not a licence; pricing not yet disclosed.

note: Agreement is described as enabling future commercial availability; no sale stated as having begun.

facts.fact: Communications Africa reports Starlink and the CAF government signed an agreement on 18 December 2025 under which Starlink's network is to be made commercially available in CAF for the first time; the document calls it an agreement, not a licence.

note: Agreement ceremony; commercial availability is future.

facts.fact: TechAfrica News (US Embassy press copy) reports Starlink and the CAF government signed an agreement on 18 December 2025 under which Starlink's network is to be made commercially available in CAF for the first time; the document calls it an agreement, not a licence.

note: Agreement ceremony; commercial availability is future.

facts.fact: Corbeau News reports a contract signed at the presidential palace between the Central African authorities and Starlink (SpaceX), after which Central Africans can subscribe to Starlink; the article gives no licence or regulator statement.

note: Free kits to isolated schools, clinics and administrations are a state-contract donation, not a fact.
